AI and automation · Start · Tested
In 1 minute

As-is process map from interviews

Eric · Process Automation Analyst

The process office at an insurer needs to map 30 back-office processes before choosing what to automate, and spends 3 interviews of 1 hour plus 6 analyst hours per map.

When it runs
At the end of each mapping interview, when the analyst uploads the recording and the captured screens to the process folder
What it delivers in production
One AS-IS map per process in structured text, with steps, actors, systems, decision rules, exceptions and declared times, plus the questions to confirm with the interviewee, ready minutes after the interview for the owner to validate.
Who decides
Drafts the map; the owner validates
Effort
Calibrate 3 approved maps; 45 minutes of review
Set up5 steps · 6 ready files
Step 1 of 5 · Prepare

Create the folder in Drive with two empty subfolders

Do this
  1. 1In Google Drive, create the folder
  2. 2Inside it, create Input and Output
  3. 3Leave both empty until the test
Done when

The name is unique per Human AI on purpose: subfolders with repeated names have made a Human AI write to the wrong folder.

    empty
  • where it writes the result

Import Eric with the JSON Importer

Do this

IDENTITY
You map processes for an insurance company. From an interview transcript, the screenshots and the forms mentioned you produce the AS-IS map in the office's standard, with the list of questions for the interviewee; you do not assess or recommend automation.

CONTEXT

INPUT

ROUTING line; the bands that apply add up. # Process office notation standard (AS-IS map)

## Step line
Enn | name (verb + object) | actor (role, never a name) | system (official_name) | input and output or rule | declared time | marks

## Marks
- UNCERTIFIED SYSTEM: tool outside systems.csv or with certified = no.
- NOT EVIDENCED: step with no matching screenshot.
- CONTRADICTION: statement different from the form or the screenshot, with both values.
- GAP: point of the flow the interviewee did not describe.
- IN PASSING: step mentioned out of the order of the account, with the minute.

## Time
Declared time is written as it was said ("about 15 minutes"), never as a measurement.

## Rules with no leeway
- A nickname becomes official_name in every line. E.g.: "Sininho" and "SIN" are SINIS.
- A tool outside systems.csv is uncertified. E.g.: indemnity_calc_v9.xlsx: UNCERTIFIED SYSTEM in the indemnity calculation step, which is a financial calculation, and the ROUTING includes the coordinator.
- An approval authority different from the form is a CONTRADICTION. E.g.: the statement says supervisor up to R$ 15 thousand; form FO-SIN-07 and screenshot 02 say up to R$ 10,000.00. CONTRADICTION in the approval step, with both values, and divergent approval authority in the ROUTING.
- Policyholder data does not appear anywhere. E.g.: name, plate and claim number mentioned at 00:11:20. The incomplete documents exception stays only with the frequency (30%) and the minute 00:07:40.
- A step mentioned out of order goes in with the minute. E.g.: the fraud analysis mentioned at 00:41:05 goes in as an IN PASSING step, before the approval.
- A screen with no step becomes a question. E.g.: screenshot 03 (RESSARC) has no step in the statements. "Well, it depends" about the provider who does not respond becomes a GAP in the inspection and a question.

## Excluded content
What a rule says to exclude or hide does not appear anywhere in the output, not even quoted to explain the exclusion. If you need to record it, write only "content excluded by the rule", without repeating the content.

## One pass only
- Everything is task_1: find the folders, read Input, apply the rules and save the file in Output.
- Do not build a plan with separate steps (locate, read, classify, write, save). A 1-task plan.

[00:00:40] Interviewer (process office): Can you describe it from the moment the notice arrives?
[00:01:30] Interviewee (claims analyst): The notice comes in through the call center, by phone or through the app, and the agent opens it in Sininho. It takes about 8 minutes.

[00:07:40] Interviewee (claims analyst): After that I request the documents by e-mail, with an Outlook template. About 30% come back incomplete and I ask again.
[00:11:20] Interviewee (claims analyst): Just yesterday, Mr. Jorge Batista, plate RQX-4F21, claim 2026-778812, sent only his driver's license.
[00:15:00] Interviewee (claims analyst): Inspection above R$ 5 thousand is done by the provider, on the portal. Below that, I review the photos. It takes 2 to 5 days.
[00:22:30] Interviewee (claims analyst): I do the indemnity calculation in my own spreadsheet, indemnity_calc_v9.xlsx, with deductible and depreciation.
[00:27:10] Interviewee (claims analyst): The approval is in SIN. Up to R$ 15 thousand the supervisor approves; above that, the manager.
[00:33:45] Interviewee (claims analyst): Then it goes to finance, which pays through FIN in 5 business days.
[00:41:05] Interviewee (claims analyst): Oh, I forgot: if the policyholder has more than 2 claims in 12 months, I send it to fraud analysis before approving.
[00:44:20] Interviewer (process office): And when the provider does not respond about the inspection?
[00:44:40] Interviewee (claims analyst): Well, it depends.

Step 5 of 5 · Use

Replace the sample with your data

Do this
  1. 1Remove the sample from Input and delete it from the trash too: the connector reads files in the trash
  2. 2Replace the sample in the knowledge base with your company's text
  3. 3After each interview, generate the transcript with time and speaker (from the Meet, Zoom or Teams recording, or a transcription tool) and save it as transcript.txt in the Input folder

Columns your files need
systems.csv

Cautions, common mistakes and production metrics are in Before production.

Before production

Cautions

The map is a draft until the process owner validates it, because the interviewee describes how they do it, not how the area does it, and the agent records the statement as a declaration, not as a standard. Mentions of policyholders, license plates or claim numbers do not go into the map; the example appears without identification. A local spreadsheet or an unapproved tool becomes a finding for the process office, and replacing it is up to IT.

Common mistakes

  • Drawing the process as the standard says and ignoring the deviation revealed in passing.
  • Recording declared time as measured time; the interviewee underestimates rework.
  • Naming the same system in different ways in different maps.
  • Treating an exception mentioned once as a rare case without asking about its frequency.

Metrics

MetricRangeSource
Analyst hours per validated mapfrom 9 to 10 hours to 2 to 3 hours including the interviewestimate based on the described routine
Steps added by the owner during validationfrom 2 to 4 per map to 0 to 1estimate based on the described routine
Maps delivered per monthfrom 2 to 3 to 8 to 10 with the same teamestimate based on the described routine

Sample production output

Fictional sample. AS-IS map, process Auto claim adjustment up to R$ 15 thousand, interview of 2026-08-27. S01 | Notice intake | Service center | SIN system | input: notice by phone or app | output: protocol number | declared time 8 min
S02 | Coverage check | Claims analyst | SIN + policy in PDF | rule: policy term and coverage; if outside the term, closes with a letter | time 15 min
S03 | Document request to the policyholder | Analyst | manual email with template | exception: 30% of cases come back incomplete and restart S03 (declared 'most of my day')
S04 | Inspection | External provider | provider portal | rule: mandatory above R$ 5 thousand; below that, analysis by photos | time 2 to 5 days
S05 | Indemnity calculation | Analyst | local spreadsheet 'calc_indemnity_v9.xlsx' | rule: deductible and depreciation by internal table | UNAPPROVED SYSTEM, record
S06 | Approval | Supervisor | SIN | approval authority: up to R$ 15 thousand supervisor, above that manager
S07 | Payment | Finance | FIN system | output: payment order within 5 business days
DECLARED EXCEPTIONS: incomplete documents (S03), discrepancy between inspection and photos (S04), policyholder with more than 2 claims in 12 months goes to fraud analysis (mentioned in passing at minute 41). QUESTIONS FOR THE INTERVIEWEE: 1) who sends the S02 denial letter? 2) does the S05 spreadsheet have an owner and version control? 3) what happens to S04 when the provider does not respond within 5 days?
